source.title: Investigating Continual Pretraining in Large Language Models: Insights and Implications
source.authors: Çağatay Yıldız; Nishaanth Kanna Ravichandran; Nitin Sharma; Matthias Bethge; B. Ermi̇ş

record.tranche_reason: The study compares perplexity across model sizes during continual pretraining and relates downstream task results to perplexity, but it does not fit or test the power-law scaling equations of the original studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports model-size/perplexity trends and downstream task outcomes. Those results do not establish a power-law curve, extrapolation accuracy, or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Reported scaling-law results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a continual domain-adaptive pretraining benchmark. It compares four off-the-shelf GPT-2 checkpoints, which have different sizes but uncontrolled training. It fits no power law, extrapolation or compute allocation. Its downstream results track one model's BIG-Bench scores across domain-shift checkpoints, not across scale or pretraining loss. It agrees with Kaplan et al. only qualitatively (larger models get lower perplexity), which is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that continual pretraining improves GPT-2 models but degrades Llama2-7B, which the authors attribute to domains being too small (<100 MB). Also add that randomized domain order improves final performance and retention, while similar order improves specialization.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines continual domain-adaptive pretraining on sequential domain corpora, rather than fitting scaling laws from runs varying parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-domain order and relevance affect outcomes; the study also reports batch-size effects on continual-pretraining dynamics.

fits_no_version.finding: In continual domain-adaptive pretraining, larger GPT-2 models achieve lower DAPT, CPT and last-checkpoint perplexity in both domain orders, and forget less. The data are figures only, with no fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: During continual pretraining, larger pretrained GPT-2 models keep lower perplexity and forget less than smaller ones.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a single model's continual-pretraining trajectory, BIG-Bench scores move with the recency and relevance of the training domain. The authors say this follows the perplexity trend, but no correlation is quantified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream task changes during continual pretraining track domain-perplexity changes and depend on the most recent training domains.

record.problems: The model-size results are presented in figures without numerical values or fitted power laws. The study reports no uncertainty estimates. The authors note that similar-order domains were ordered only once and that some results may be affected by training-data overlap for RoBERTa.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were omitted.

untested.parts: No power-law fit. The size ordering comes from 4 pretrained GPT-2 models with no controlled parameter, token or compute sweep.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Continual pretraining is studied, but no power-law form is tested in that regime.
No downstream performance measured across model sizes or against pretraining loss across scaled runs.
No exponents or fitting choices compared.

record.verdict_notes: The paper labels a section 'Scaling laws for continual pretraining', but it only reports a monotone size ordering among four GPT-2 checkpoints. It cites Kaplan et al. as agreeing. Downstream analysis covers only GPT2-M and Llama2-7B, never a size sweep. No study-level verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits or exponents; no scaling over tokens or compute; no test of the claimed power-law shape over several orders of magnitude.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or comparison of parameter and token growth with compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Continual pretraining is studied, but the study does not test whether a power-law form holds in that regime or in other modalities and training regimes.
No broad prediction from pretraining loss or scale to downstream performance across independently scaled runs; downstream outcomes are tracked across continual-pretraining stages.
No comparison of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices; no test of curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: Llama2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated BIG-Bench downstream tasks at continual-pretraining checkpoints.

conditions.value: Arithmetic, General Knowledge, Physics, CS Algorithms, and Few-shot NLG

rows.value: figure only; text reports scores often below GPT-1 and a drastic decline after the first task, regardless of task or order
rows.note: The authors say these downstream trends follow the same trend as perplexity; the result is reported collectively across tasks.
rows.check: Llama2-7B scores collapse to roughly chance after continual pretraining. This shows degradation under domain training, not predictability with scale. Marking it 'observed' for V6 was wrong.
